messages:
maria: Quick brain-dump — we need to move from single 'per-model-family' hard caps to something that understands size tiers (small/medium/large) and lets orgs borrow short bursts across tiers. The ask is: enforce predictable cost/latency constraints per org while allowing controlled burst UX.
kevin: +1. Do you mean enforcing separate quotas like tokens_small, tokens_medium, tokens_large? Or a shared budget with weighted drains?
maria: Prefer a hybrid: primary allotments per tier + a small shared overflow pool that can be borrowed for N minutes with a payback multiplier. Reason: avoids blocking devs on spikes but keeps unit economics sane.
dmitri: Implementation notes: routing needs model_size tag in the request (e.g., header X-Model-Size: medium) so quota middleware can classify. Runtime already emits model metadata but gateway currently strips that. We should preserve/forward it.
kevin: Enforcement point debate: API gateway (fast reject) vs runtime (precise token accounting). My vote: gate at gateway for fast negative, but also deduct at runtime to avoid double-spend if request routes across multiple nodes.
maria: Agreed. Gateway does fast token-bucket check + reserve a provisional hold. Runtime finalizes consumption when tokens are actually emitted (so we need an idempotent finalize call).
dmitri: That implies a two-stage flow: /v1/requests -> gateway reserves N tokens -> attach reservation-id -> runtime finalizes and returns actual tokens_consumed. If runtime consumes < reserved, refund the difference to quota pool.
kevin: Sketch of quota config (yaml):

```
quota_policies:
  org_default:
    small_tier: 1000000   # tokens/month
    medium_tier: 300000
    large_tier: 50000
    overflow_pool: 50000  # shared tokens
    overflow_window: 300  # seconds
    overflow_multiplier: 1.5  # cost multiplier for borrowed tokens
```

anika: UX thoughts: Console should show per-org stacked area chart (small/medium/large + overflow usage) with hover showing effective cost after multiplier. Also allow admins to set per-api-key overrides and a toggle to disable overflow borrowing.
maria: Telemetry we need:
- quota.reserve (labels: org_id, key_id, model_tier, reserved_tokens)
- quota.finalize (labels: org_id, key_id, model_tier, tokens_consumed)
- quota.refund (labels...)
- quota.limit_hit (labels: org_id, key_id, model_tier, reason=hard|overflow_exhausted)

kevin: Metric names look good. Also emit histogram of reserve_latency and finalize_latency so we can SLO the quota path.
dmitri: Edge cases: streaming responses where tokens aren't known upfront. For streaming, gateway reserves a small initial bucket and runtime periodically checkpoints consumption to extend reservation. If finalize never arrives (crash), we need TTL-based reclamation.

sre-bot: incident:quota: note that last-week spikes in eu region consumed overflow for many small-tier apps; we saw unexpected cost shift. Recommend alert: overflow_utilization > 80% for 10m.

maria: Policy question: should overflow borrowing be unlimited across tiers (eg large -> small) or only downgraded models (large requests can borrow small pool?) My take: only allow upward borrowing (small/medium borrow from adjacent bigger tiers is risky w.r.t latency/cost). Better: allow borrowing from lower-cost tiers only if model is exact match — hmm confusing.

kevin: I'd constrain borrowing to same-or-smaller tier only if *serving* a smaller model as fallback. For example: if medium is saturated, route to small (cheaper) and charge lower tokens rather than borrowing large-tier pool.
maria: Right — separate mechanisms: borrowing (temporary extra capacity at higher cost) vs fallback routing (serve a cheaper model variant). Both should be configurable per-org.
dmitri: Implementation tasks (rough):
- add model_size header propagation (gateway -> runtime)
- build quota service endpoints: /reserve, /finalize, /refund
- gateway integration to call /reserve synchronously
- runtime finalize & periodic checkpointing for streaming
- TTL-based reclamation job
- metrics + alerts

anika: Console tasks:
- per-org quota page with tier breakdown
- controls for overflow toggle, multipliers, and per-key overrides
- alerting UI for overflow thresholds

maria: Decision: go forward with hybrid model (per-tier allotments + small overflow pool + repay multiplier). Reserve/finalize flow for accuracy. We will prototype with a 3-day experimental rollout to 10% of orgs.

kevin: Action items (owners):
- kevin: prototype gateway reserve integration + YAML config parser (ETA: 1w)
- dmitri: runtime finalize + streaming checkpoints (ETA: 2w)
- anika: console mockups for tier view and overflow toggle (ETA: 1w)
- maria: draft rollout plan + billing implications doc (ETA: 3 days)

maria: @kevin please create RFC PR with the config schema and reserve/finalize API spec. Keep it light, we can iterate.
kevin: Will do. filing PR now :+1:

sre-bot: deploy-bot: quota-service v0.3 deployed to staging at 2026-03-15T10:12:31Z :rocket:

maria: thanks everyone — this thread captures the shape. We'll iterate on edge cases in the RFC.
